question: A nurse finishes changing a wound dressing on a patient with MRSA surgical site infection. The used dressing, blood-soaked gauze, and gloves should be disposed of in which container?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Under BMW Rules 2016, blood/body fluid-soaked dressings, gauze, and gloves contaminated with infectious material are Category 2 soiled waste. Yellow bags are designated for incineration or autoclaving followed by shredding.

White puncture-proof containers are exclusively for sharps — needles, scalpels, broken glass (Category 3). Soft items like dressings and gloves are not sharps; they belong in yellow bags as soiled/infectious waste.

Blue bags are designated for discarded glassware, metallic body implants, and pharmaceutical/cytotoxic waste. Blood-soaked dressings from an infected wound are soiled/infectious waste (Category 2) and require yellow bag disposal.

Materials contaminated with blood or infectious body fluids are biomedical waste under BMW Rules 2016 and must never enter the general municipal waste stream. Yellow bags ensure proper treatment by incineration or autoclaving.

overallFeedback.feedback: Blood-soaked dressings, gauze, and contaminated gloves are Category 2 soiled/infectious waste under BMW Rules 2016. They must be placed in yellow bags for incineration or autoclaving + shredding.
Yellow bags are the correct disposal route for all soiled and infectious waste (Category 2) under BMW Rules 2016 — segregation must happen at the point of generation.
